figures.title: Chapter map
figures.why: the chapter is one equation Kmax = hf - phi plus one wavelength λ = h/p
figures.read: every result is the photon's energy-momentum bookkeeping or the wave it carries to matter

figures.title: The photoelectric apparatus as a current-voltage map
figures.why: the retarding voltage is a filter, sweeping away electrons from fastest to slowest
figures.data: the evacuated-tube circuit: light onto emitter, retarding collector, ammeter/voltmeter
figures.read: below threshold no light triggers emission; at threshold only the collector voltage changes

figures.title: The five facts and the two that destroy waves
figures.why: three facts look like wave behaviour, two do not - separating discriminators from decoys
figures.data: the five experimental facts of §3.2 against the classical wave prediction
figures.read: threshold, instantaneity, and Kmax ∝ f rule out waves; current ∝ intensity cannot decide
figures.source: §3.2 The experimental facts and the classical predictions they destroy

figures.title: Triage - route by the keyword
figures.why: the keyword names the equation before any number is touched
figures.read: emission is photon bookkeeping, diffraction is matter waves, a size is uncertainty

figures.title: Kmax versus frequency for two metals
figures.why: the shared slope h/e across every metal measures Planck's constant; intercepts are work functions
figures.data: Kmax = hf - φ: two parallel lines, slope h/e, thresholds f0(Cs)≈4.6e14 Hz, f0(Zn)≈10.4e14 Hz
figures.read: common slope h/e for every metal; cesium turns on first because its φ is smaller

figures.title: de Broglie wavelength: the classical world is the geometry limit
figures.why: the same formula describes a cricket ball and a neutron; wave is visible only when λ meets lattice spacing
figures.data: λ = h/p on a log axis: ball ~1e-34 m, neutron ~1.8 Å, electron ~0.12 nm, spacing 0.1-1 nm
figures.read: wave behaviour shows only when λ is comparable to the geometry it meets
